intent: EXPLICIT: Provide a service that converts long URLs into short, shareable codes, redirects visitors from the short code to the original URL, persists all mappings durably, and records/report usage analytics for each short URL. INFERRED: The system must be architected so it could realistically evolve toward higher-scale production deployment, not just work as a one-off script.

functional_requirements.label: EXPLICIT
functional_requirements.text: Provide an API to create a short URL from a given original URL.

functional_requirements.label: EXPLICIT
functional_requirements.text: Provide a mechanism to redirect a client from a short code to the original URL.

functional_requirements.label: EXPLICIT
functional_requirements.text: Provide analytics about short URL usage (at minimum redirect/usage counts).

functional_requirements.label: EXPLICIT
functional_requirements.text: Persist URL mappings so they survive process restarts.

functional_requirements.label: INFERRED
functional_requirements.text: Reject or reject-with-error invalid input URLs rather than silently accepting them.

functional_requirements.label: INFERRED
functional_requirements.text: Return a clear error for unknown/nonexistent short codes.

functional_requirements.label: ASSUMED
functional_requirements.text: Resubmitting the same original URL should not create unbounded duplicate rows; the existing mapping should be returned instead (idempotent creation).

functional_requirements.label: ASSUMED
functional_requirements.text: Short URLs may optionally expire; expired short codes must not redirect successfully.

non_functional_requirements.label: EXPLICIT
non_functional_requirements.text: The service must be 'scalable' — the requirement explicitly uses this word.

non_functional_requirements.label: INFERRED
non_functional_requirements.text: The service must be maintainable: layered code (API / business logic / persistence / analytics), not a single monolithic file.

non_functional_requirements.label: INFERRED
non_functional_requirements.text: The service must be testable end-to-end (unit, integration, API, failure-path tests).

non_functional_requirements.label: ASSUMED
non_functional_requirements.text: For this prototype, single-node SQLite persistence is acceptable; true horizontal scalability is a documented future-evolution concern, not a prototype requirement.

non_functional_requirements.label: ASSUMED
non_functional_requirements.text: No authentication/authorization is required for the prototype (public-style URL shortener), since none was requested.

constraints.label: EXPLICIT
constraints.text: Must run on Python 3.11+, FastAPI, SQLite, pytest per repository-level project constraints.

constraints.label: EXPLICIT
constraints.text: No Docker, Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure, external database, or external LLM/API may be used.

constraints.label: EXPLICIT
constraints.text: Implementation must remain small/maintainable, consistent with a ~20 hour interview-prototype scope.

dependencies.text: None — this is a greenfield build with no existing repository to integrate with.

ambiguities.text: No concrete numeric scale target (requests/sec, users, data volume) was provided for 'scalable'.
Whether URL creation should be restricted to authenticated users was not specified.
Whether short URLs expire by default, and after how long, was not specified.
Whether analytics should include only aggregate counts or per-request details (IP, user agent, referrer) was not specified.
Behavior when the same original URL is submitted twice was not specified.

assumptions.text: Treat 'scalable' as an architectural-evolution requirement: the prototype must be stateless-service-shaped and documented with a clear path to load-balanced/horizontally-scaled deployment, rather than requiring a specific throughput to be benchmarked in this prototype.
No authentication is implemented in the prototype; this is called out as a known limitation and future evolution item.
Expiration is optional per-URL (nullable field), not enforced by default; if set, redirect returns 410 Gone once expired.

Analytics are limited to aggregate redirect_count, created_at, and last_accessed_at, plus a per-redirect event log (timestamp only) for basic trend analysis. No IP/user-agent capture, to avoid unnecessary privacy/security surface in the prototype.
Resubmitting an identical, non-expired original URL returns the existing short_code (HTTP 200) instead of creating a duplicate row.

unknowns.text: Whether short codes must be human-readable/pronounceable or purely random is not specified; random base62 codes are used as a reasonable default.
Long-term analytics retention policy is not specified; no automatic pruning is implemented in the prototype.

acceptance_criteria.text: POST /urls with a valid http(s) URL returns 201 with a unique short_code and short_url.
POST /urls with a malformed or non-http/https URL returns 422 with an error detail.
POST /urls with an original_url that already has an active mapping returns 200 with the existing short_code (idempotent), not a new row.
GET /{short_code} returns a redirect (302) to the original URL when the code exists and is not expired.
GET /{short_code} returns 404 for an unknown short code.
GET /{short_code} returns 410 for a short code that exists but has expired.
GET /urls/{short_code}/analytics returns short_code, original_url, created_at, redirect_count, and last_accessed_at for a known code, and 404 for an unknown code.
Each successful redirect persists an increment to redirect_count and updates last_accessed_at durably (verified by restarting the process/reopening the DB).
Source code is organized into distinct API, service, repository, model, and analytics layers (not a single file).
The full pytest suite executes successfully via `python -m pytest` with zero failures.
